heroSummary: While the Bambu Lab A1 Mini can achieve printing speeds up to 202 mm/s at a 17 mm³/s volumetric flow limit, printing Sunlu ASA requires an advanced setup due to the printer's 80°C maximum bed temperature and open-frame design. Achieving reliable adhesion without delamination necessitates using an external draft shield or enclosure cover and strong bed adhesives.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with Magigoo or PVP Glue Stick
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed at 17 mm³/s in the filament profile to match the flow limit and prevent under-extrusion at high speeds.
Set Bed Temperature to the maximum 80°C for all layers and increase First Layer Extrusion Width to 0.5 mm for enhanced mechanical bed grip.
Enable an OrcaSlicer Draft Shield around the model to trap convective heat and block open-frame room airflow.
Set part cooling fan between 0% and 20% max, keeping the fan entirely off for the first 4 layers to maximize layer bond strength.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe Corner Lifting and Bed Detachment
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Bed temperature capped at 80°C (below ASA ideal of 90-105°C) combined with open-air ambient convective drafts.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply PVP glue stick or specialized adhesive on Textured PEI, add an 8-10 mm outer brim with 0 mm brim-object gap, and enable a tall draft shield.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive auxiliary/part cooling airflow and low ambient printing chamber temperature inducing thermal shrinkage stress.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Disable auxiliary cooling fans, cap part cooling fan at 15-20% only for extreme overhangs, and raise nozzle temperature to 260°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Ooze, Stringing, and Rough Surface Blobs
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorbed by hygroscopic ASA filament leading to steam expansion inside the hotend melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the Sunlu ASA spool in an active filament dryer at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours prior to printing and verify retraction is set to 0.6 mm.

faq.question: Can I place an enclosure over the Bambu Lab A1 Mini for printing ASA?
faq.answer: Yes, a lightweight thermal tent helps retain heat, but keep internal ambient temperatures below 45°C to prevent motherboard and power supply electronics from overheating.

faq.question: Is the 80°C bed temperature sufficient for large Sunlu ASA prints?
faq.answer: The 80°C bed is marginal for ASA; large footprint prints will inevitably lift at the corners unless kept to small dimensions or securely brimmed in a draft-free environment.

faq.question: Do I need a hardened steel nozzle to print Sunlu ASA on the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: No, standard Sunlu ASA is non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle installed on the A1 Mini will handle this material without accelerated wear.

faq.question: Is it safe to print Sunlu ASA in an unventilated indoor room?
faq.answer: No, ASA releases styrene fumes and ultrafine particles during printing, requiring either an outdoor exhaust duct, an active carbon filter, or dedicated workshop ventilation.
